post_template.hook_style: Open with a direct, locally anchored question or bold statement tied to East Auckland autumn urgency or interest rate movement — both confirmed as highest-relevance themes across all five April 2026 research briefs and carried forward into May 2026 as seasonal and economic context remains unchanged. The three highest-engagement Facebook posts in the period (scores of 3, 2, and 2) were all image posts published at 08:00, 11:00, and 10:00 respectively, confirming the hook must work in tandem with a strong visual and a morning or mid-morning publish time. Top-performing hook patterns drawn from research briefs and aligned with brand voice guide: 'Thinking of selling this autumn? Here is what most East Auckland homeowners miss.' or 'The rate cut just changed the game — here is what it means for your home.' or 'Before you wait until spring, read this about the East Auckland market.' or 'Most sellers do not know what waiting until winter actually costs them.' or 'This is what a premium East Auckland result actually looks like in 2026.' Hook must appear in the first line before any line break. East Auckland geographic anchoring is mandatory — generic national openers flagged across all five research briefs as a format to avoid and must never be used. Interest rate cuts and autumn listing urgency remain the two highest-confidence hook themes for this period and must anchor at least two hooks per week across all platforms. Behind-the-scenes and personal brand hooks remain elevated as a weekly priority given the complete and ongoing absence of this format from the archive across all recorded periods. New for this update: a second morning time slot at 11:00 is now confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and must be incorporated as a third scheduling window alongside 08:00 and 10:00 — the archive has never tested morning posting across any of the 17 recorded posts which all defaulted to 20:00.
post_template.structure: hook → value or education point → local East Auckland relevance → soft CTA
post_template.best_performing_format: LOW CONFIDENCE — Facebook reach and impression data returned zero across all 23 posts analysed in the insights period, consistent with an API or data collection issue rather than true zero organic performance. The three highest raw engagement scores (3, 2, and 2) were all from image posts published at 08:00, 11:00, and 10:00 on April 19, April 29, and April 28 respectively, confirming image format combined with morning and mid-morning scheduling as the strongest available engagement signal in this period. All 17 archived local posts in the local_archive were text-only with zero image or video content recorded — a critical and ongoing format gap that has now persisted across three consecutive strategy periods despite being identified as the most urgent tactical change in each prior update. This text-only pattern directly contradicts brand identity visual guidelines and the format recommendations of all five research briefs. Based on April 2026 research data across five separate briefs, image posts with lifestyle-driven visuals and education-focused captions are the recommended primary format. Short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format across multiple research briefs and must be introduced as a weekly priority on Instagram Reels and TikTok without further deferral. Text-only posts are deprioritised to a maximum 25 percent of weekly output. Image-to-text ratio target is 3:1 minimum and must be treated as non-negotiable from this week forward.

image_strategy.overlay_style: Short punchy headline overlay in brand black (#000000) or brand white (#FFFFFF) placed on clean negative space areas of the image — maximum 2 to 6 words per overlay aligned with brand voice guide. Subtle brand red (#C8102E) used sparingly as an accent on key words, underlines, or thin divider elements only — never as a full background. Compositions must intentionally include negative space at the top or bottom third for overlay placement. Examples aligned to voice guide: 'Sell smarter.', 'This one won't last.', 'East Auckland living.', 'Buy with confidence.', 'Your next move starts here.', 'Don't overpay.', 'The window is closing.' Overlay text must never cover the primary visual selling feature of the image. Font weight must be bold and legible at mobile screen sizes.
